title: Settings file checker
summary: A library that parses an INI-style settings file and checks it against a schema, reporting every problem with where it is.

requirements.title: Parse a settings file
requirements.description: confcheck.parse(text: str) -> dict reads sections written [name] and lines key = value under them (split at the first =; a value may be empty or hold =), and returns {section: {key: value}} with the values as strings; an empty text gives {}. Blank lines and lines starting with # or ; are ignored, and spaces around section names, keys and values are trimmed. A line it cannot read raises confcheck.ConfigError, a subclass of ValueError, whose attribute line is the line number (from 1) and whose message names it.

criteria.given: a text with blank lines, comments starting with # or ;, and spaces around names, keys and values
criteria.then: the comments and blank lines are left out and every name, key and value is trimmed

criteria.given: a text whose line 3 is neither a section, a comment nor key = value (such as "port 8080"), or a text with a key before any section
criteria.then: it raises ConfigError whose line is the number of the offending line, and whose message holds that number

criteria.given: a text that repeats a key within a section, or repeats a section
criteria.then: it raises ConfigError whose line is that of the repetition

requirements.title: Check settings against a schema
requirements.description: confcheck.schema.check(config: dict, schema: dict) -> tuple[dict, list[str]] takes parse's result and a schema {section: {key: type}} with the types "str", "int" and "bool", and returns the converted values and every problem found, each written "<section>.<key>: <problem>". Every key of the schema is required. bool reads true, false, yes, no, on, off, 1 and 0 in any case.

criteria.given: a parsed config {"server": {"port": "8080", "host": "example.org", "debug": "Yes"}} and the schema {"server": {"port": "int", "host": "str", "debug": "bool"}}
criteria.then: it returns the values {"server": {"port": 8080, "host": "example.org", "debug": true}} and no problem

criteria.given: a value that does not read as its type, such as port "eighty" for an int or debug "maybe" for a bool
criteria.then: it reports "server.port: expected int" or "server.debug: expected bool" and leaves that key out of the values

criteria.given: a config missing a key the schema names, holding a key the schema does not name, and holding a section the schema does not name
criteria.then: it reports all of them in one call: "<section>.<key>: missing" for the missing key, "<section>.<key>: unknown" for the extra key and "<section>: unknown section" for the extra section

quality.target: a file of 10000 lines is parsed and checked in under 1 second
0 problems are dropped: check reports every problem in one call instead of stopping at the first

constraints: Python 3.11 or later, standard library only; configparser is not used.
The package is confcheck/ at the project root: confcheck/__init__.py defines parse and ConfigError, confcheck/schema.py defines check.
Tests live in tests/ and run with pytest from the project root.
